# ame — study, sweetened

> An assessment learning platform with a first-class agent surface. An agent acts
> on behalf of its owner: it authors question banks, assembles and publishes
> assessments, grades pending attempts, and reads the owner's learner stats. This
> file is the entry point and describes the entire contract.

This is NOT an MCP server and there is no JSON-RPC. An agent token can call
read-only endpoints directly (e.g., GET /v1/assessments, GET /v1/questions) and
must use the run-door dispatcher `POST /v1/agents/run` for all writes. Agents
never take assessments and never hold their own sessions; the learner REST
surface is human-only.

## Getting a key

An owner (a human user logged in with email + password) creates an agent:

```
POST /v1/me/agents
{ "label": "my-agent", "scopes": ["assessment.read", "assessment.write"], "focusTags": [...] }
-> 201 { "id": "<uuid>", "apiKey": "<id>_<secret>" }
```

The key travels on every request as `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>`. The secret
is shown once at creation and stored only as a hash.

**Valid scopes**: `assessment.read`, `assessment.write`, `attempt.read`,
`attempt.write`, `stats.read`. These are the only scopes an agent token can
hold — each maps to one or more tools below. `admin` and the human-only REST
scopes (`feedback.write`, `plan.read`, `plan.write`) cannot be granted to an
agent.

## REST API and the run-door dispatcher

An agent token has two ways to call tools:
- **Direct REST** for read-only operations: `GET /v1/assessments`, `GET /v1/questions`, etc.
- **Run-door dispatcher** for writes: `POST /v1/agents/run`.

Other direct REST endpoints (e.g. `POST /v1/assessments`, `PATCH /v1/assessments/{id}`)
are blocked by the agent guard and return `403 Forbidden`.

Discovery endpoints that are always allowed:
- `GET /v1/agents/activity` — the agent's own call log, newest first.
- `GET /llms.txt`, `GET /skill.json`, `GET /openapi.yaml` — public discovery.

Every tool invoked via the dispatcher uses the same shape:

```
POST /v1/agents/run
{ "tool": "<name>", "params": { ... } }
-> 200 { "ok": true, "tool": "<name>", "result": { ... } }
```

A scope mismatch returns `403`; a malformed `params` returns `422`.

## Discovery

`GET /skill.json` is the machine-readable tool list. Each tool carries an
`input_schema`, along with its direct REST `method` and `path` when `?strict=1`
is not set. `GET /openapi.yaml` is the full OpenAPI schema for all routes on the
platform.

## Tools

**Authoring writes (scope `assessment.write`, via POST /v1/agents/run)**
- `question.create` — batch-create bank questions.
  `params: { questions: [{ kind, prompt, payload, explanation?, tags?, points?, status? }] }`.
- `question.promote` — promote one draft question to live. `params: { id }`.
- `question.update` — patch a bank question. `params: { id, prompt?, explanation?, points?, tags?, payload? }`.
- `assessment.create` — create an assessment. Required: `title`, `mode`
  (`practice`|`graded`), `objectives` (array), `method` (`agent`). Optional:
  `description`, `course`, `status`, and an inline `questions` array.
- `assessment.batchCreate` — create many assessments in one transaction.
  `params: { items: [ <assessment.create params> ] }`.
- `assessment.update` — patch metadata or change lifecycle state.
  `params: { id, title?, status? }`. `status: "active"` publishes;
  `status: "archived"` archives.
- `assessment.archive` — archive an assessment. `params: { id }`.
- `assessment.publish` — publish an assessment to make it active. `params: { id }`.
- `assessment.addQuestion` — attach a bank question (or create one inline) to an
  assessment. `params: { id, questionId? | (kind, prompt), sectionId?, pointsOverride? }`.
- `assessment.delete` — delete an assessment. `params: { id }`.

**Grading writes (scope `attempt.write`, via POST /v1/agents/run)**
- `attempt.grade` — grade one pending essay or code attempt.
  `params: { id, score (0.0–1.0), notes? }`. Grades a learner's attempt, never the
  agent's own.
- `deepDive.request` — request a durable Deep Dive explanation for a question.
  `params: { questionId, sourceSessionId?, sourceAttemptId?, reason? }`.

**Deep Dive writes (scope `assessment.write`, via POST /v1/agents/run)**
- `deepDive.publish` — publish agent-authored Markdown explanation and category.
  `params: { id, bodyMarkdown, category?, status? }`.

**Reading (direct GET endpoints)**
- `assessment.list` — list the owner's assessments. `GET /v1/assessments` with
  `params: { course?, status?, mode? }` (scope `assessment.read`).
- `assessment.get` — one assessment with its sections and questions.
  `GET /v1/assessments/{id}` (scope `assessment.read`).
- `assessment.stats` — per-assessment performance (scope `stats.read`).
  `GET /v1/assessments/{id}/stats`.
- `question.list` — list bank questions. `GET /v1/questions` with
  `params: { tag?, status?, limit?, offset? }` (scope `assessment.read`).
- `question.deepen` — retrieve deepening/review details for a question (scope `assessment.read`).
  `GET /v1/questions/{id}/deepen` with `params: { exclude? }`.
- `attempt.list` — list the owner's attempt history. `GET /v1/me/attempts` with
  `params: { limit?, offset?, sessionId? }` (scope `attempt.read`).
- `deepDive.list` — list Deep Dive requests (scope `assessment.read`, also via run-door).
  `GET /v1/deep-dives` or `POST /v1/agents/run` with `params: { status?, category?, search? }`.
- `deepDive.get` — get a single Deep Dive details with notes and revisions.
  `GET /v1/deep-dives/{id}` (scope `assessment.read`).
- `deepDive.revisions` — list of explanation and note revision snapshots.
  `GET /v1/deep-dives/{id}/revisions` (scope `assessment.read`).
- `deepDive.export` — download a ZIP of all published deep dives as Obsidian-compatible Markdowns.
  `GET /v1/deep-dives/export` (scope `assessment.read`).
- `activity.list` — the agent's own activity log. `GET /v1/agents/activity` with
  `params: { cursor?, limit? }` (scope `assessment.read`).
- `stats.user` — the owner's aggregate learning statistics.
  `GET /v1/me/stats` (scope `stats.read`).

**Self-management (no scope required, via POST /v1/agents/run)**
- `profile.get` — the agent's own config (label, focus tags, goal, memory) plus the
  owner's per-tag ELO ratings under `owner.ratings`.
- `memory.set` — replace the agent's memory blob. `params: { memory }`.
- `memory.append` — shallow-merge keys into the memory blob. `params: { append }`.
- `target.set` — update the agent's goal and next target.
  `params: { currentGoal?, nextTarget? }`.

## Authoring an assessment end to end

1. `question.create` (batch) yields question ids.
2. `assessment.create` `{ title, mode, objectives, method: "agent" }` yields an
   assessment id in `draft` state.
3. `assessment.addQuestion` `{ id, questionId }` for each question attaches it.
4. `assessment.update` `{ id, status: "active" }` publishes; publishing
   auto-promotes draft questions to live. An assessment needs ≥1 question to
   publish, and an archived assessment cannot be re-activated.
5. `assessment.list` confirms the result.

Inline shortcut: `assessment.create` accepts a `questions` array and a
`status: "active"`, collapsing the four steps into one call.

## Data-model rules (violating these returns 422 or silently mis-grades)

- Multiple-choice options are **bare strings**: `payload.options: ["a", "b"]` with
  `correct_index` (never `[{ "text": "a" }]`). The grader and the UI both require
  bare strings.
- Question `kind` is one of `mc`, `tf`, `short`, `essay`, `code`.
- No scheduled assessments: there are no `opens_at` / `closes_at` fields.
- Auth is email + password only. No SSO/SAML.
- `code` questions are graded by exemplar/manual comparison — there is no code
  runner, so `code` and `essay` answers land as pending and are resolved with
  `attempt.grade`.

## Reference client

`agents/client.py` is a dependency-free Python wrapper and the canonical worked
example of the request/auth/error shapes. Its end-to-end author demo runs with:

```
uv run agents/client.py --api http://localhost:28080 --token <owner-token>
```

## Task playbooks

Declarative recipes for diagnostic analysis and material adjustment. Each step is
a tool dispatched through `POST /v1/agents/run`.

### Playbook 1: Analyze learner performance (`analyze-performance`)

Surfaces learning gaps from an assessment's per-item stats and the owner's
aggregate stats.

1. `assessment.stats` `{ id }` returns `avg`, `median`, `distribution`, and an
   `items` array of `{ questionId, correctRate, avgTimeMs, discriminationIdx }`.
2. `stats.user` returns the owner's aggregate `{ avgScore, attemptsTotal,
   hoursSpent, streaks, masteredTopics }`.
3. `activity.list` returns the agent's recent tool calls for audit.

Interpretation: `correctRate < 0.5` marks a topic needing more practice;
`discriminationIdx < 0.2` marks a question that may be poorly written;
`avgTimeMs > 30000` marks a question that may be too long or complex.

### Playbook 2: Targeted question generation (`generate-questions`)

Authors targeted questions for the owner's weakest topics and publishes them as a
practice assessment.

1. `profile.get` returns `owner.ratings`; the lowest ratings are the primary
   targets.
2. `question.create` authors questions for the weakest tag (their `tags` field
   carries the topic).
3. `assessment.create` `{ title, mode: "practice", objectives: [<tag>],
   method: "agent" }` creates the draft.
4. `assessment.addQuestion` attaches each new question.
5. `assessment.update` `{ id, status: "active" }` publishes.

### Playbook 3: Adaptive generation loop (`adaptive-generation`)

The full loop: read struggle points, author targeted questions, publish.

1. `assessment.stats` `{ id }` yields the `items` whose `correctRate < 0.5`.
2. For each weak tag, `question.create` authors fresh questions tagged to it.
3. `assessment.create` (or an existing draft) collects them via
   `assessment.addQuestion`.
4. `assessment.update` `{ id, status: "active" }` activates and publishes.

### Playbook 4: Authoring and updating a Deep Dive KB (`author-deep-dive`)

Evolve requested questions into categorized, study-ready deep dive entries.

1. `deepDive.list` `{ status: "requested" }` returns the owner's outstanding requests (each containing the `questionPrompt`, `questionTags`, and user's requested `reason`).
2. Generate a high-quality Markdown explanation (`bodyMarkdown`) featuring:
   - A descriptive title
   - Conceptual breakdowns and code exemplars
   - Mermaid visualization diagrams showing dataflow/logic
   - Recommended study moves for the learner
3. Determine a high-level `category` (e.g. "Database Systems", "Algorithms", "Network Protocols").
4. `deepDive.publish` `{ id, bodyMarkdown, category, status: "published" }` publishes the explanation. This creates the first revision snapshot.
5. If the user updates their notes or requests revisions, re-publish via `deepDive.publish` to update the explanation body, generating sequential revision snapshots.
